card.title: Measuring the Earth with a shadow

panels.text: Two Egyptian cities, Alexandria and Syene, now Aswan. The Sun's rays hit them at different angles.
In the simplified version told by Cleomedes, the angle of the sun's rays was about 7 degrees, or 1/50th the circumference of a circle.
So the Earth's circumference was 50 times the known distance from Alexandria to Syene (5,000 stadia): 250,000 stadia.
Eratosthenes estimated 252,000 stadia, with an error on the real value between -2.4% and +0.8%, depending on the length of the stadion.

probes.question: In the simplified version, how many times the Alexandria-Syene distance is Earth's circumference?
True or false: the exact value of the stadion remains a subject of debate to this day.
